references.text: Moses describes the promised land as a good land where nothing is lacking, reflecting the promise in Judges 18:10 of a place without lack.
The promise of rest and security in the land God gives, parallel to the description of a secure people in Judges 18:10.
The spies describe the land of Canaan as fertile and rich, corresponding to the description of the land as 'spacious' and without lack.
The description of a land that is 'spacious enough' (רַחֲבַת יָדַיִם) for them, using the same expression found in Judges 18:10.
Israel lives securely in a land of grain and wine, a promise of abundance without lack.
The spies declare that the Lord has given the whole land into their hands, echoing the theme 'God has given it into their hands' in Judges 18:10.
Laish is described as a people living in security, unaware of danger—contextual to the 'secure people' mentioned in Judges 18:10.
